name: Abiathar
bio:
Abiathar was the son of the priest Ahimelech. When Saul, acting on Doeg's report, ordered the massacre of the priests of Nob, Abiathar alone escaped, fleeing to David with an ephod in hand (1 Samuel 22:20; 23:6). He told David that Saul had slaughtered his father's household; David, grief-stricken, said, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul... I am responsible for the death of your whole family," and promised him protection: "Stay with me; don't be afraid. The man who wants to kill you is trying to kill me too. You will be safe with me" (1 Samuel 22:21-23).

From then on, Abiathar stayed close to David, carrying the ephod as the priest through whom David inquired of the LORD during his years as a fugitive — as at Keilah, where David used the ephod Abiathar brought to learn of Saul's plan to besiege the city (1 Samuel 23:6-12). Once David's kingdom was secure, Abiathar served alongside Zadok as priest in David's royal administration (2 Samuel 8:17).

When Absalom's rebellion forced David to flee Jerusalem, Abiathar went out with Zadok and the ark, but David sent the priests back into the city, choosing to trust the LORD's will rather than treat the ark as a talisman for his own safety. David asked Abiathar, along with his son Jonathan, to stay behind and relay to him anything they could learn of Absalom's plans (2 Samuel 15:24-29, 35-36). Abiathar continues to play an important role through David's rise to the throne and into the reign of Solomon, a story told in detail through the rest of Samuel and into 1 Kings.
